subject: Recap + integration requirements and procurement owners
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@clairhealth.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clairhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + integration requirements and procurement owners

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into procurement: 

Key decision criteria we heard today
- Latency: p95 inference target <= 250ms for user-facing queries (goal: <200ms on dedicated capacity for small payloads).
- Cost: target blended inference cost <= $0.15 per 1k tokens for expected steady-state workload (see notes on batching below).
- Deployment: prefer Dedicated (reserved GPU) for production; Private/VPC for any PHI scope.
- SLA: 99.9% availability target, with SLOs on tail latency and a rollback/fallback policy.

Security/legal/procurement notes
- ClairHealth requires SOC2 evidence and a security questionnaire (they requested the abbreviated summary during the call).
- Procurement will need an initial SOW + PO template; expect a 4–6 week procurement window once SOW + pricing are approved.

Owners and immediate next steps
- Logan (me): share SOC2 summary + post-demo slides (attached).
- Ben Carter: lead procurement thread and share PO template / pricing deck.
- Marissa Cole: own security questionnaire responses and technical control evidence.

Attachments: post-demo-deck.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Proposed timeline: draft SOW + pricing by Aug 20; procurement kickoff (PO/terms) week of Aug 24.

Two quick clarifying questions for you, Emily / Tom: who on your side is the economic buyer (finance or procurement contact)? And is there a preferred procurement contact/email we should send the SOW to?

Thanks — Logan

--
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@clairhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + integration requirements and procurement owners

Thanks Logan — really helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

> Key decision criteria we heard today
> - Latency: p95 inference target <= 250ms for user-facing queries (goal: <200ms on dedicated capacity for small payloads).

Can you confirm whether the 250ms p95 target is expected when routing through our app layer + network (i.e., end-to-end), or is that the pure service-side inference p95? Our infra team will want a network-included number for SLA planning.

Also: Tom is our VP Eng and will be the economic buyer on the engineering/ops side; procurement@clairhealth.com should be the PO contact. Finance (CFO) will be looped for larger commitments but Tom is the decision owner for technical/ops spend.

One more: does Redwood support Private (on-prem) installs if we land PHI requirements, and do you have a rough delta in costs between Dedicated vs Private? A high-level number is fine for planning.

Thanks — Emily
Director of Applied AI, ClairHealth
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@clairhealth.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clairhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + integration requirements and procurement owners

Great questions — thanks Emily. Quick answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

On Aug 19, 2026, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@clairhealth.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether the 250ms p95 target is expected when routing through our app layer + network (i.e., end-to-end), or is that the pure service-side inference p95?

- The latency numbers in my bullets were service-side inference p95 (Redwood runtime only). For procurement/SLA purposes we should capture both:
  - Service-side inference p95 target: <= 200–250ms (depending on model selection & batch config).
  - Typical end-to-end (app + network) add ~30–80ms depending on region and our outbound path — recommend you baseline from your staging infra.

> Does Redwood support Private (on-prem) installs if we land PHI requirements, and do you have a rough delta in costs between Dedicated vs Private?

- Yes, we support Private (VPC and on-prem deployments). Ballpark delta: Private deployments have additional engineering + licensing costs — typically 20–40% premium over Dedicated reserved capacity depending on integration/support level. We’ll include a more precise estimate in the SOW draft.

Next steps (action owners):
- Ben: attach PO template + initial pricing scenarios (do this by Aug 20).
- Marissa: send the short-form security evidence (SOC2 controls mapping + questionnaire answers) and the full control repo link.
- Logan: prepare SOW draft + integration appendix (network routing, expected latency numbers by model).

Links: HubSpot deal CL-3479: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/CL-3479

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up with Tom and procurement if that helps speed the timeline. 

Thanks — Logan
